chunks: Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Barqi wrote to Abu Jaʿfar al-Thani عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, is prayer behind one who stopped at your father and your grandfather عليهما السلام permissible?”
So he replied: “Do not pray behind him.”

key_terms.أَبِيكَ: your father, referring to the Imam’s father عليه السلام
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), specifically congregational prayer in this context
key_terms.جَدِّكَ: your grandfather, referring to the Imam’s grandfather عليه السلام
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind, meaning in following an Imam in prayer
key_terms.لَا تُصَلِّ: do not pray, a direct prohibition
key_terms.وَرَاءَهُ: behind him, meaning under his leadership in prayer
key_terms.وَقَفَ: stopped short, referring to halting at a limited acceptance of the Imamate

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat behind someone who stopped at accepting only certain Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question addressed to Imam Abu Jaʿfar al-Thani عليه السلام about the permissibility of praying behind someone who halted at the Imamate of the Imam’s father and grandfather. The Imam عليه السلام gives a clear ruling forbidding prayer behind such a person, indicating the significance of correct belief in religious leadership within congregational prayer.
